pages.title: Boltzmann Brains & Poincaré Recurrence
pages.text: $(thing)Boltzmann Brains & Poincaré Recurrence$()$(br2)A dead universe is not quite dead. In a finite system at equilibrium every state comes back, given time, and fluctuations out of equilibrium happen by pure chance - a star, a planet, a brain. Unlocks the Boltzmann Fluctuation.

$(thing)Insight$(): 260$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Heat Death, Thermodynamics of Information.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Heat Death Ember.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A small part of a universe at equilibrium, at temperature T, can fluctuate by chance into a state with a little more energy (by Δ_E) and a little less entropy (by Δ_S) than it should have. The probability falls off exponentially in the free energy the fluctuation needs, measured in units of k_BT. Write the probability.
